content.title: About
content.content: Cashews are the edible seeds of the cashew tree (Anacardium occidentale) native to tropical regions. Honey roasted cashews are coated with a thin layer of caramelized honey, giving them a sweet aroma and crunchy texture. They can be enjoyed as a snack or used in cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cashews are not true nuts botanically; they are seeds attached to the fruit’s "apple."
Tropical climate and well‑drained soils promote optimal growth of cashew trees.
Cashews are widely used in Asian cuisines, especially Thai and Indian dishes.
Honey roasting enhances sweetness while preserving most nutrients.
Cashews are rich in iron, zinc, and copper, essential trace minerals.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Cashews contain monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: One cup of cashews provides about 15 g of protein, beneficial for muscles and tissues.

items.title: Contains magnesium and copper
items.content: These minerals aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cashews are a good source of niacin (B3) and riboflavin (B2), supporting metabolic processes.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phenolic compounds and vitamin E in cashews help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Cashews can trigger allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Due to their energy density, they should be consumed in moderate portions.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Cashews contain oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in predisposed people.

items.title: Added sugar in honey‑roasted version
items.content: The honey coating raises sugar levels, so people with diabetes should account for it.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cashews can be eaten as a snack, added to muesli, yogurt, salads, baked goods, or used in sauces. Honey roasted cashews are especially tasty in desserts and granola mixes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cashews in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent the fats from becoming rancid.

chocolate-candy-with-nuts-other-nfs.title: Chocolate candy with nuts, other, NFS

content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate candy with nuts is a sweet treat made of milk or dark chocolate that incorporates whole nuts (almonds, hazelnuts, cashews, etc.) or nut paste. The product falls under the “other” category and carries the NFS code 5082. It offers a classic combination of sweet chocolate and crunchy nuts, making it a popular confection.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first chocolate‑nut candies appeared in Europe in the 19th century.
The pairing of chocolate and nuts enhances the release of aromatic compounds, creating a richer flavor.
Nuts are often coated with a thin layer of chocolate, protecting them from oxidation.
In many countries these candies are a traditional gift for holidays and celebrations.
NFS code 5082 is used in customs and statistical systems to classify such sweets.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Nuts provide monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa in chocolate and polyphenols in nuts have antioxidant properties that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Nuts supply magnesium, iron, and zinc, important for metabolism and immune function.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: The combination of chocolate carbohydrates and nut fats offers lasting satiety and energy.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Chocolate stimulates serotonin and endorphin production, helping to improve mood.

items.title: Nut allergy
items.content: These candies can trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to nuts.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive sugar may contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Chocolate nut candies are energy‑dense, so they should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Dark chocolate contains caffeine, which can affect sleep if consumed in large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Candies can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to dessert platters, used in baking, or as a garnish for cakes. For young children, offer finely chopped pieces to reduce choking risk.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the candies in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep them in an airtight container to prevent moisture absorption and maintain crispness.

content.title: About
content.content: A chocolate doughnut is a small fried or baked sweet bun coated with a dark or milk chocolate glaze. It combines a soft, airy dough texture with the rich flavor of cocoa, often enhanced with a cream, jam, or fruit filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Doughnuts appeared in the United States in the early 1920s and quickly spread across Europe.
Chocolate doughnuts are frequently decorated with sprinkles, nuts, or caramel drizzles.
In some countries doughnuts are shaped as rings, while in others they are solid “filled” discs without a hole.
Traditional preparation involves deep‑frying, but modern recipes often bake them to reduce fat content.
There are countless filling options, from classic vanilla cream to fruit mousses.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The carbohydrate content provides a quick boost of energy, making it a convenient snack.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa in the chocolate glaze is rich in flavonoids, which may support cardiovascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole‑grain dough can supply B1, B2, and niacin, which aid metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chocolate doughnuts can contribute iron, magnesium, and zinc when made with nutrient‑dense ingredients.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Sugar and theobromine in chocolate stimulate serotonin production, potentially enhancing mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of tooth decay.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Fried doughnuts contain saturated and trans fats, which may negatively affect cholesterol levels.

items.title: Gluten and dairy allergies
items.content: Traditional recipes use wheat flour and dairy, making the product unsuitable for those with related allergies.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: One chocolate doughnut can contain 250–400 kcal, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chocolate doughnuts are best enjoyed fresh and slightly cooled. They can be eaten as a standalone dessert, paired with coffee or milk, or used as a base for ice‑cream sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store doughnuts in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2–3 days. For longer storage, keep them in the refrigerator (up to a week) or freeze them after wrapping tightly in plastic film.
